A Flaw is you promising the table that your character will make things harder for themselves, and the system promising to pay you for it.

This is the part of 20 Below that most needs saying out loud: the game gets better when things go wrong, and it’s built to reward you for letting them. A Flaw isn’t a penalty you swallowed for points. It’s a hook you handed the GM, and every time they pull it, you get paid.

Flaws are chosen at creation and hand points back to spend elsewhere. Taking one means it’s going to come up, and it’ll cost you something real when it does. If a Flaw never once inconveniences you, it wasn’t a Flaw - it was a discount, and somebody at the table should say so.

Flaws are Boons in a mirror - the complications, quirks and bad hands you pick on purpose.

**Every Flaw is Leveled, 1 to 5**, the same way Resources are, and the Level is the price. Take Amnesia at 3 and you get 3 points back; at 5, you get 5. Nothing here is bought flat.

**They’re rarely a number.** A Flaw is usually a complication or a restriction rather than a minus-something on a roll. The few that do carry numbers say so themselves.

**You take them at creation, and only at creation.** This is a bargain you strike while you’re building, not one you can come back for.

**A Flaw that never bites is worth nothing.** If it doesn’t actually make life harder, it isn’t a Flaw and it doesn’t pay - the one-eyed character with no depth perception problem and no trouble it has ever caused them, which is a common enough trope, doesn’t collect for Impaired Senses on the strength of an eyepatch.

## The Flaws

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Amnesia</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

There’s a shape in your history where something used to be. You’ve stopped poking at it, mostly.

</div>

Part of your past is missing.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A single traumatic event is missing - one specific memory gone, everything else intact.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A cluster of related memories is missing - the days or weeks around a specific incident, or one relationship entirely forgotten.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>A significant span of time is missing - months or years, not just one moment. Name, identity, and abilities are intact, but real gaps exist in personal history and relationships.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Most personal history is gone - only fragments remain. Still knows their own name and can act normally, but life before a certain point belongs to a stranger.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Forgotten their entire identity - may not know what Skills or Boons/Gifts they have.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Antagonist</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

Somebody out there is thinking about you right now, and not fondly.

</div>

Someone or something is set against you - a rival, an enemy, a hunter who doesn’t give up.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A minor rival - someone who competes with or needles you personally. Low capability, mostly a nuisance.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A capable individual enemy, or a small hostile group/local authority keeping an eye on you.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>A well-resourced enemy or organized hostile group actively working against you.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>A powerful, dangerous enemy or organization with real reach, actively hunting you.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>A nemesis-tier antagonist - extremely powerful, far-reaching, and personally invested in your downfall. Relentlessly hunts you as a top-priority target.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Anxiety</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

The threat assessment never switches off. Most of what it reports is wrong, and knowing that has never once helped.

</div>

Anxiety that doesn’t need a reason and doesn’t switch off.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A specific, narrow fear or recurring nightmare - unsettling, but rarely interferes with function.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A phobia that actively triggers avoidance or hesitation when confronted with its source.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Generalized anxiety - chronic worry and disrupted sleep color everyday decisions, not just one trigger.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Panic attacks - sudden, incapacitating episodes of panic under stress, not just avoidance.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>A pervasive anxiety disorder - constant hypervigilance, frequent panic attacks, and deeply entrenched avoidance that fundamentally limits day-to-day life.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Berserk</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

There’s a point past which you stop making decisions and start just continuing.

</div>

Once you’re going, you don’t stop until it’s over.

Each level’s effect is cumulative - it keeps every lower level’s restriction and adds its own.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>Once triggered by real danger, cannot voluntarily disengage from the current fight - must keep engaging until an enemy is defeated or flees.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Level 1, plus: while triggered, cannot declare a Slow Action Bracket - full aggression only, no called shots or concentration.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Levels 1-2, plus: must always act against the nearest hostile target - no picking tactically who to engage.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Levels 1-3, plus: the trigger doesn’t end just because the original threat is gone - any new hostile that appears keeps the fight going.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Levels 1-4, plus: keeps fighting even when badly hurt - won’t retreat or stop to protect themselves, only stopping when physically unable to continue (unconscious, restrained, or no hostiles remain).

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Code of Conduct</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

There’s a line, and you’ve never crossed it. That has cost you, and it will again.

</div>

A rule you set yourself and won’t break, even when breaking it would help.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A minor, low-stakes personal restriction - inconvenient, rarely costly. Strict vegetarian/vegan; never tells even a white lie; always pays a debt the moment it’s owed; won’t enter a home uninvited.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A real behavioral rule that occasionally costs something. Never draws a weapon first; refuses payment for helping someone in genuine need; never abandons a task once started, however small; always keeps a promise made to a friend.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>A binding code that actively shapes major decisions. Once I draw my blade, it must taste blood; any promise made must be kept regardless of personal cost; a formal challenge, once accepted, can’t be walked away from; a secret entrusted to them is kept even under real pressure.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>A severe restriction that limits options in dangerous or critical moments. Refuses to harm anyone significantly weaker than themselves; an enemy must always be given a chance to surrender before a killing blow; cannot break a vow even to save their own life.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>An absolute, life-defining restriction. I cannot kill anything, no matter the cost; a vow that cannot be broken under any circumstance, even to save the people they love; can never refuse a genuine request for help, regardless of personal danger.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Dependent</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

Somebody’s safety is stitched to yours. They didn’t ask to be, and neither did you.

</div>

Someone relies on you, and has to be protected or provided for.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A dependent who mostly manages on their own - checks in occasionally, needs a little financial or emotional support now and then.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A dependent who needs regular, real support - time, money, or care on a recurring basis, though not helpless.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>A dependent who can’t protect themselves and needs real intervention when trouble finds them - a young child, an elderly parent, someone seriously ill.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>A dependent who is a frequent liability - regularly endangered by your own life (enemies, work, reputation), requiring real risk to protect.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>A dependent who is entirely helpless without you and a prime target - enemies know exactly who to threaten to get to you.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Destitute</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

Money is a thing that happens to other people. You’ve gotten very good at the arithmetic of not having it.

</div>

You have no money - anywhere from a bad patch to nothing at all.

Each level’s effect is cumulative - it keeps every lower level’s complication and adds its own.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A rough patch. Creation-Wealth is **0** instead of the default 2 for gear shopping at creation, and no Resources Pool or Discretionary points may be spent on Wealth while this Flaw is held - buy it off first - see Everyman Gear Packages for what’s still available at Level 0. Doesn’t follow you past creation; whatever put you here (a lost job, a bad breakup, a bad month) is already turning around.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Chronically tight. As Level 1, and it doesn’t go away - living paycheck to paycheck, or with no paycheck at all, is an ongoing fact of your life, however your Resources ended up built.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Real precarity. As Level 2, and something concrete is currently unstable - unreliable housing, an unreliable income source, or a debt actively being chased.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Genuinely impoverished. As Level 3, and it’s visible enough that people react to it on sight - shapes first impressions the same way Notable Appearance or Notoriety do, just for money instead of looks or reputation.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Nothing left. As Level 4, and there’s no safety net at all - no one to call for a loan, no fallback plan, and whatever put you here is bad enough to be a real, ongoing story hook (GM’s call on specifics).

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Directionless</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

Everyone else seems to keep a map running somewhere behind their eyes. You never got issued one.

</div>

You get lost. Reliably.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A mildly unreliable sense of direction - occasionally turns around even in familiar places, rarely costs more than a moment.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A poor sense of direction - regularly gets turned around in unfamiliar areas, needs to double-check directions rather than trust instinct.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Actively bad - gets lost even in semi-familiar places without a map, guide, or other aid to follow.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Severe - cannot reliably navigate even short, familiar routes without external aid; easily disoriented under any pressure or unfamiliar layout.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>No functional sense of direction whatsoever - completely dependent on others or tools to get anywhere; could get lost in their own home under stress or darkness.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Fragile</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

Your body keeps a longer memory of damage than other people’s do.

</div>

The body works against you.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>Mildly delicate - bruises easily, tires a bit faster than average, but functions fine day to day.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Noticeably weaker - real physical exertion (lifting, running long distances) is harder, minor injuries take a bit longer to heal.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Frail - the body struggles under real exertion or stress; a condition flares up under pressure; recovery from harm is markedly slow.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Seriously compromised - sustained exertion risks real harm; even routine physical demands can trigger a flare-up or setback; wounds that would be minor for others become serious.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>The body is failing - barely able to sustain ordinary physical demands without real risk; any injury is dangerous and slow to heal; a single hard fight could be life-threatening regardless of what actually connects.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Gun-Shy</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

It starts, and there’s a gap between when you should move and when you do.

</div>

When violence starts, you falter.

Each level’s effect is cumulative - it keeps every lower level’s penalty and adds its own.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>First round of combat, act last within your declared Action Bracket, regardless of Initiative.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Level 1, plus: for the first round, Fast actions are treated as Normal and Normal actions are treated as Slow - Slow actions can’t be taken that round at all.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Levels 1-2, plus: unless 1 Ki is spent, they don’t act at all in the first round of combat.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Levels 1-3, plus: while in combat, they act at Disadvantage.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Levels 1-4, plus: the Ki-to-act requirement from Level 3 applies every round, not just the first - without spending Ki each round, they’re frozen entirely; when they do act, it’s at Disadvantage throughout.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Illiterate</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

The letters are right there and they don’t resolve. You’ve built a whole life around not needing them to.

</div>

You can’t read, to one degree or another.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>Illiterate only in the local language/script - fully literate (possibly exceptionally so) in their own.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Illiterate in every language/script they’re likely to encounter while traveling, though still fully literate at home - the gap is broader than just “here.”

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Only semi-literate even in their native language on top of that - basic reading/writing is possible, but real fluency isn’t there anywhere.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Functionally illiterate everywhere, including their own native language - cannot meaningfully read or write at all.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>No concept of written language whatsoever - doesn’t register that symbols represent language in the first place.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Impaired Senses</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

One of the channels is down, and you’ve rerouted around it well enough that people forget - right up until it matters.

</div>

One of your senses is dulled, or gone.

**A reminder of the general rule above**: if the impairment doesn’t actually impair you - no depth-perception penalty, no missed cues, nothing a compensating sense or trained-around habit doesn’t fully cover - it isn’t worth points. This Flaw is the most obvious anime-trope case for that rule (the one-eyed swordsman who fights exactly as well as anyone with two eyes).

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A minor gap in one sense - reduced but functional (mild nearsightedness beyond normal correction, slight hearing loss in one ear, a dulled sense of smell). Real but manageable.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A significant impairment in one sense - noticeably worse than normal, actively affects tasks that rely on it, but not total loss (poor low-light vision, muffled hearing, no sense of smell at all).

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Total loss of one sense - fully blind in one eye, fully deaf in one ear, or a complete loss like smell/taste. Other senses compensate, but real gaps remain.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Total loss of a primary sense - fully blind or fully deaf, relying entirely on other senses and/or tools/training to compensate.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Total loss of multiple primary senses - both blind and deaf, or similarly extreme. Complete reliance on remaining senses and outside support.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Incantations</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

It doesn’t work if you can’t say it. Something out there is listening for the words specifically.

</div>

A Gift of yours only works if you can say a specific phrase out loud.

A Gift only answers to a spoken word - distinct from a Gift’s own Limiters like Animal Friendship’s Vocal Component: this is a full character-creation Flaw, its points added to the general Flaws total like any other, chosen against one or more Gifts you already have.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>One specific Gift requires speaking a short trigger phrase aloud to activate - audible to anyone nearby, and it simply doesn’t work if you’re unable to speak (silenced, gagged, underwater, and the like).

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>The phrase grows more specific - a full sentence, verse, or exact wording - long and distinct enough that garbling or rushing it fails the activation outright.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Two or more Gifts each require their own spoken incantation to activate.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Every Gift you have requires its own spoken incantation - none of your capability works if you can’t speak clearly.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>As Level 4, and the incantation must be spoken clean, with no other exertion that Round - sprinting, grappling, or taking a hit while attempting one fails it outright, forcing you to start over next round.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Item of Power</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

The thing you can do isn’t entirely in you. Some of it is in an object, and objects can be taken.

</div>

A Gift of yours lives, at least partly, in something you carry rather than in you.

Your capability isn’t fully your own - it lives, at least in part, in something you carry. Distinct from a Gift’s own Limiters (which discount that specific Gift’s point cost): this is a full character-creation Flaw, its points added to the general Flaws total like any other, chosen against one or more Gifts you already have.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>One specific Gift only works while you’re in possession of a particular item - well-secured or hard to casually separate from you (a tattoo, an implant, something bonded to you), but losing it locks out that one Gift entirely until it’s recovered.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>As Level 1, but the item is a real, ordinary object - a ring, a blade, a pendant - that can be stolen, confiscated, or lost in a struggle like any other possession.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Two or more Gifts are bound to the same item instead of just one - losing it locks out everything tied to it at once.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Every Gift you have depends on retaining the item - lose it, and you’re left with nothing but your ordinary Skills, Boons, and Attributes until it’s recovered.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>As Level 4, and the item itself is something genuinely easy to take, damage, or lose - not secured, not bonded, not hard to separate from you at all. Anyone who thinks to try has a real shot at disarming you completely.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Lame</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

The distance is the same as it always was. It just costs more now.

</div>

An old injury or condition took some of your mobility and kept it.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A minor limp or stiffness - noticeable, doesn’t slow them down in any real way.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Reduced mobility that costs something under exertion - slower over distance, real effort on stairs or rough terrain.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>A significant mobility loss - needs a cane, brace, or similar aid for anything beyond short, easy movement.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Severe impairment - mobility is a constant limiting factor; sustained or fast movement is difficult even with aids.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Effectively immobile without significant support - a wheelchair or equivalent, or unable to move under their own power at all in a fight or chase.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Notable Appearance</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

People remember you. Every single time, whether that’s useful or not.

</div>

Something about how you look draws stares and reactions.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A minor, easily-overlooked trait - noticed only on close attention, rarely commented on.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A distinctive feature that people notice and occasionally remark on, but doesn’t follow them.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>A memorable appearance that people recognize and remember on sight - recall and gossip travel with them.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>A striking appearance that draws stares and comment everywhere, actively makes blending in impossible.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>An unmistakable, singular appearance - described in wanted posters and rumors alike; anyone who’s heard of them would recognize them on sight.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Notoriety</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

Your name arrives in the room before you do, and it’s already said something you’d rather it hadn’t.

</div>

How widely, and how badly, you’re known.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>Known within a small local circle - a minor local bad reputation, occasional suspicion.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A known troublemaker within a community or subculture.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Regionally known for something bad - distrust follows them beyond their home turf.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Widely infamous - recognized and reviled by strangers regularly.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>A notorious name nationwide or worldwide, actively shunned or targeted on reputation alone.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Overconfident</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

You’ve been right often enough to stop checking, which is a habit with a shelf life.

</div>

You underestimate danger, or overestimate yourself, and you do it consistently.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>Occasionally shrugs off a real warning - rarely costs anything, mostly just talk.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Regularly takes on tasks slightly beyond them without checking first - real but recoverable setbacks.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>You habitually dismiss genuine danger and sound advice, and it costs you, and sometimes your allies, real setbacks.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Reliably walks into situations that are clearly beyond them, refusing help or backup even when it’s obviously needed.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Cannot recognize danger as danger until it’s already too late - repeatedly puts themselves and others at serious risk through sheer refusal to see their own limits.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Pariah</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

There’s a category people put you in on sight, and no amount of being reasonable gets you out of it.

</div>

People hold a specific prejudice against you - your species, your background, where you came from.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A minor prejudice - occasional dirty looks, mild social friction, rarely any material consequence.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Real but limited discrimination - some doors are harder to open (served last, passed over for a room), but nothing blocks basic life.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Active, meaningful discrimination - regularly denied service, employment, or fair treatment; public spaces mean dealing with real hostility.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Systemic hostility - the prejudice has institutional teeth: denied legal protection, actively targeted by local authority, barred from whole industries or areas.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Widespread, violent hostility - openly hunted, attacked, or persecuted for what they are; public life is dangerous.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Reliance</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

There’s a thing you need, and the needing has its own schedule.

</div>

Something you need - a compulsion, a substance, or a condition that has to be managed.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A minor compulsion or mild reaction - inconvenient, rarely costly. A nervous habit like nail-biting; a mild seasonal allergy; a harmless lucky ritual before anything risky.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A real pull or trigger that occasionally costs something. A gambling habit that drains resources; an allergy requiring real caution (shellfish, bee stings); a compulsive need for background noise or routine that disrupts focus when broken.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>A genuine dependency that shapes daily life. Regular substance use requiring a fix on a schedule; a chronic condition needing daily management (insulin, medication); hoarding or obsessive behavior that actively strains relationships.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>A severe dependency with real danger if unmet. Hard addiction with physical withdrawal symptoms; a severe, life-threatening allergy on exposure; a compulsion strong enough to override better judgment in the moment.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>A life-controlling dependency. An addiction that incapacitates without regular access; a condition requiring constant, uninterruptible support to survive; a compulsion so absolute it defines every decision you make.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Ritual Required</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

It answers, but not immediately. There’s a procedure, and the procedure takes as long as it takes.

</div>

A Gift doesn’t answer the instant it’s reached for - it has to be called, coaxed, or earned each time.

Your power doesn’t answer the instant you reach for it - it has to be called, coaxed, or earned each time. Distinct from a Gift’s own Limiters: this is a full character-creation Flaw, its points added to the general Flaws total like any other, chosen against one or more Gifts you already have.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>One specific Gift requires a short ritual - roughly a minute of chanting, gestures, or preparation - before its first use each Scene. Once performed, that Gift stays primed and usable normally for the rest of the Scene.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>The same Gift now requires that ritual before every single use, not just once per Scene - each activation costs the full minute of setup again.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>The ritual itself grows heavier - roughly ten minutes, real focus required. Anything that would normally cause Distracted interrupts it outright, forcing you to start over.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Every Gift you have requires the Level 3 ritual before its first use each Scene, not just one - priming your full capability takes real, dedicated time.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Every Gift requires the full ritual before every single use, with no priming grace at all - full setup, every time, for everything you can do.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Secret</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

One fact, and a life built carefully around it not coming out.

</div>

Something you badly don’t want getting out.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>An embarrassing detail - mildly damaging to reputation if it got out, nothing more.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A real secret - exposure would cost you something genuine: a relationship, a job, a bit of standing.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>A serious secret - exposure would cause real, lasting damage to your life, or the lives of people you care about.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>A dangerous secret - exposure invites real threats: legal jeopardy, violence, or being hunted by someone with the power to act on it.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>A world-shaking secret - exposure would be catastrophic, reshaping your life entirely, or endangering far more than just you.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Shaken Confidence</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

Something happened once, in front of people, and some part of you never quite got up from it.

</div>

One specific humiliation took your footing in a room, and you never got it back.

One specific, defining humiliation left a real mark - not on the body, on the nerve. A natural fit for the genuine Flaw a below-zero Poise scar can impose, though it can also just be taken directly at creation like any other Flaw.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A specific type of social situation (public speaking, a rivalry, one particular person) triggers a flicker of doubt - costs a beat, nothing more.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Real hesitation in that situation - a genuine, recoverable setback if pushed through anyway.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Active avoidance of that situation where possible; forced into it, performs at a real disadvantage.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>The doubt bleeds into adjacent situations, not just the original trigger - a broader loss of confidence.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>A pervasive, crippling lack of social self-assurance - even routine interactions carry real hesitation, not just the original trigger.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Short Fuse</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

There’s a shorter distance than most people have between the provocation and the response.

</div>

You anger fast, and everybody can tell.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>Snaps at minor annoyances - sharp words, nothing lasting.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Loses composure under real provocation - says or does something they regret, with real (if recoverable) social cost.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Hard to talk down once provoked - regularly escalates situations that a calmer head could have defused.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>A serious liability under pressure - provocation reliably leads to real damage: burned bridges, real consequences, sometimes violence.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>You can’t reliably control yourself once triggered - provocation regularly leads to serious harm, to relationships or to people, with real consequences you can’t walk back.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Soft-Hearted</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

You know what the tactical answer is. You’ve simply never been able to make yourself give it.

</div>

You struggle to act against the vulnerable, even when it costs you.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>Hesitates for a moment before acting against someone clearly weaker or in distress - costs a beat, nothing more.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>Actively looks for a way to avoid harming the vulnerable, even if it costs real effort or a worse outcome elsewhere.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>Will take a genuine risk or loss rather than harm someone vulnerable - a real, recurring cost.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>Cannot bring themselves to act against the vulnerable even when the stakes are severe - will let an opportunity or advantage slip away rather than cross that line.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Will actively endanger themselves or the mission to protect or spare someone vulnerable, every time, no exceptions.

</div>

</div>

<div class="flaw" markdown="1">

<p class="flaw-name" markdown="span">Speech Impediment</p>

<div class="flaw-flavour" markdown="1">

The thought is clear and fast. Getting it out is the part that isn’t.

</div>

A stutter, an accent, something that gets between you and being understood.

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--1" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">1</span>A mild, noticeable quirk (a stutter under stress, a thick accent) - rarely actually hampers being understood.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--2" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">2</span>A real impediment that occasionally causes miscommunication or draws unwanted attention.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--3" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">3</span>A significant impediment - regularly slows or garbles speech enough that real effort is needed to be understood.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--4" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">4</span>A severe impediment - verbal communication is unreliable; often misunderstood or unable to get a full thought out under pressure.

</div>

<div class="flaw-level flaw-level--5" markdown="1">

<span class="flaw-n">5</span>Effectively unable to communicate verbally in any reliable way - must rely on writing, gestures, or another person to speak for them.

</div>

</div>
